structured_output.hypothesis: If paired bovid horns are conjugate mirror-image spirals, then in per-individual measurements the left and right horns of the same animal will have equal length, basal circumference and spiral parameters (pitch, twist), differing only by small, non-directional random error, with opposite handedness.
structured_output.pass_criterion: In a per-individual dataset with separate left and right horn measurements from at least 30 adults of a spiral-horned bovid, the mean absolute left-right difference in horn length is below 2% of mean horn length. In addition, the mean signed difference is not significantly different from 0 (paired t-test p > 0.05), and at least 95% of individuals show opposite helical handedness on the two sides.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The mean absolute left-right difference in horn length is 5% or more of mean horn length, OR the paired test shows significant directional asymmetry (p < 0.01) with an effect size above 2% of mean length, OR more than 5% of individuals show the same helical handedness on both horns.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's "conjugate spirals" and "mirror-image" are read as: equal size and shape on the two sides, with opposite chirality. Measurable quantities are left and right horn length along the outer curve, basal circumference, and 3D helix parameters from landmarks or scans. Under a modern reading, fluctuating asymmetry of a few percent is tolerated as measurement and developmental noise, but directional or antisymmetric asymmetry would count against the claim. The test needs per-side data on individual animals. Species-level maxima, as in published trophy tables, cannot decide it.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: No suitable public per-individual dataset with separate left and right bovid horn measurements could be found and fetched. Searches of Dryad and the wider web returned only datasets that do not record per-side horn values. Examples are Tidière et al. 2020 on ontogenetic horn-length allometry, and a dataset on female horn investment that uses species-level maxima from Bovids of the World. The left-right asymmetry studies I found (Catalan goat horns, mouflon trophies, domestic sheep skull geometric morphometrics) appear as journal articles or institutional repository records. I could not confirm a downloadable raw data deposit for any of them. I opened no dataset landing page, and I name no identifier I did not verify.
